spec.doc: Runs atomically at deploy time, so nobody can front-run initialization. `protocol_fee_share_bps` is the default protocol/LP split for new markets; 10_000 keeps the whole fee with the protocol (pre-upgrade behaviour). Pass 0 to give all fees to the market creators.
spec.name: __constructor

spec.doc: The market's snapshotted breakers (`None` for legacy markets created before breakers existed — those are never checked).
spec.name: breaker_config

spec.doc: The current ledger's band reference, if a band check has run this ledger. `None` means the next trade sets the reference (to its own pre-trade price, which equals the ledger-open price).
spec.name: breaker_state

spec.doc: Spend `collateral_in` to buy `outcome` shares. Returns shares received. Reverts if fewer than `min_shares_out` would be received. Legacy entrypoint: no deadline and no limit price, so a signed bound can execute at any later time. Prefer `buy_v2`.
spec.name: buy

spec.doc: `buy` plus a deadline (`env.ledger().timestamp()` seconds — network time, not the client clock) and an average-price limit (`limit_price_bps` per share, 1.0 = BPS; 0 = no limit). The average price includes the fee (`fee` is part of `collateral_in`) and, for a NO buy, is compared against the NO price. Because the deadline check runs before `require_auth`, an expired transaction fails cheaply. A limit above BPS can never pass for a buy and is rejected as invalid.
spec.name: buy_v2

spec.doc: The creator (the LP) claims their share of accrued trade fees at any time, including before finality. Returns the amount claimed (0 when nothing is pending, mirroring `sweep_fees`).
spec.name: claim_lp_fees

spec.doc: Creator (the LP) withdraws whatever the pool still holds once final, plus any unclaimed LP fees. Returns the total paid out.
spec.name: claim_pool_remainder

spec.doc: Claims the LP pool remainder for up to `MAX_BATCH` markets the `creator` owns, with one collateral transfer. Same ordering and skip semantics as `redeem_many`. A market closed by `finalize_market` reports `AlreadyClaimed` — the sweep already took the remainder.
spec.name: claim_pool_remainders

spec.doc: Creates a market and seeds the pool. `creator` becomes the sole LP. `initial_yes_bps` in [100, 9900] sets the opening YES probability; the creator receives the leftover shares of the likelier outcome.
spec.name: create_market

spec.doc: Permissionless close-out of a final market after its redemption deadline. Sweeps the market's entire remaining balance — value reserved for shares never redeemed, an unclaimed LP remainder, per-holder rounding dust and accrued fees — to the treasury, and marks the market closed so nothing can ever pay out again. The deadline is `redeem_deadline(market_id)` = `finalized_at + horizon_secs`, the horizon being snapshotted at creation from the admin default. Anyone who redeems before the deadline is paid the exact `settle_value` they would have received without this call; only shares still unredeemed at the deadline are forfeit, and their value goes to the treasury rather than the LP so the LP cannot profit from suppressing redemptions. Returns the amount swept. The swept total is exactly the market's contract balance: sets plus fees minus everything already paid out.
spec.name: finalize_market

spec.doc: Spot price of `outcome` in bps (0..=10_000). YES + NO ~ 10_000.
spec.name: get_price

spec.doc: Largest accepted `market_ids` length for `redeem_many` / `claim_pool_remainders`. Frontends should chunk work into strictly ascending batches of at most this size (see `docs/frontend-integration.md`).
spec.name: max_batch

spec.doc: Cumulative YES-price-seconds as of `now - seconds_ago`. The accumulator is piecewise linear in time (the price only moves when a trade lands), so between observations the value is interpolated along the chord, and times after the last trade extrapolate at the last traded price. Fails with `ObservationTooOld` when `seconds_ago` reaches before the oldest surviving observation (the ring keeps the most recent 16), and with `NotSupported` for markets created before the accumulator existed. A missing (archived) ring slot is skipped, never a panic.
spec.name: observe

spec.doc: The pending admin proposal, including its expiry, if one exists.
spec.name: pending_admin

spec.doc: Cumulative `price_bps * seconds` for YES since creation, extrapolated to now: `observe(market_id, 0)`. Ready-made for consumers that store their own checkpoints and compute TWAPs off-chain.
spec.name: price_cumulative

spec.doc: Starts a two-step handover of the admin role. The new admin must call `accept_admin` itself, so a typo cannot hand control to an address nobody holds.
spec.name: propose_admin

spec.doc: Affects markets created after the call and the legacy fallback in `sweep_fees`. Markets with a snapshotted `FeeTerms` keep paying their original recipient.
spec.name: propose_treasury

spec.doc: Shares a `buy` of `collateral_in` would return right now.
spec.name: quote_buy

spec.doc: Shares a `sell` for exactly `collateral_out` would consume right now.
spec.name: quote_sell

spec.doc: Pays out `holder`'s position for a final market and clears it. Losing positions clear with a payout of 0.
spec.name: redeem

spec.doc: Timestamp after which unredeemed shares are forfeit (see `finalize_market`). `None` while the market is still Open — its deadline is not known yet — and for legacy markets, which have no deadline and cannot be finalized.
spec.name: redeem_deadline

spec.doc: Redeems `holder`'s positions across up to `MAX_BATCH` final markets with one collateral transfer. `market_ids` must be strictly ascending (`InvalidAmount` otherwise; empty or over-cap is `BatchTooLarge`) so the footprint is deterministic and duplicates are impossible. Markets that cannot pay do not abort the batch; they come back in `items` with a `SkipReason`. In particular an archived `Market` entry is NOT `NotFound` — the transaction fails at footprint time and the market must be restored first (simulation shows this before submission). `holder.require_auth()` covers the whole batch: the signed payload is the `market_ids` vector itself.
spec.name: redeem_many

spec.doc: Receive exactly `collateral_out` by selling `outcome` shares. Returns shares sold. Reverts if more than `max_shares_in` would be needed. Clients turn "sell N shares" into `collateral_out` off-chain (see `math::calc_sell` docs) and add a slippage margin to `max_shares_in`. Legacy entrypoint: no deadline and no limit price. Prefer `sell_v2`.
spec.name: sell

spec.doc: `sell` plus a deadline (ledger timestamp, seconds) and a minimum average execution price (`limit_price_bps` per share, 1.0 = BPS). A zero limit is trivially satisfied for sells — unlike buys, where 0 means "no limit" — and a limit above BPS can never pass, so neither needs a special case. The average includes the fee, which the trader pays out of the gross.
spec.name: sell_v2

spec.doc: Sets the breaker defaults copied into markets created after the call. `band_bps < max_impact_bps` (both non-zero) is rejected: a single trade that is allowed by the impact cap could then never fit inside the band, locking trading.
spec.name: set_default_breaker

spec.doc: Affects markets created after the call; existing markets keep their fee.
spec.name: set_default_fee_bps

spec.doc: Affects markets created after the call; existing markets keep the horizon snapshotted at their creation. Must be within [180 days, 1825 days].
spec.name: set_default_redeem_horizon

spec.doc: Affects markets created after the call; existing markets keep the split they snapshotted at creation.
spec.name: set_protocol_fee_share_bps

spec.doc: Outstanding-share accounting for a market (issue #14). `NotSupported` for markets created before this bookkeeping existed.
spec.name: settle_state

spec.doc: Anyone can move accrued protocol fees to the market's fee recipient. Sends to the recipient snapshotted in `FeeTerms` at creation. Markets created before `FeeTerms` existed have none and keep the legacy behaviour: the `DataKey::Treasury` of the moment of the sweep.
spec.name: sweep_fees

spec.doc: Transfers the single LP role (the right to `claim_pool_remainder` and `claim_lp_fees`) to `new_creator`. Only until the remainder has been claimed; after that the role has no remaining value.
spec.name: transfer_lp

spec.doc: Moves `amount` shares of `outcome` from `from` to `to`.
spec.name: transfer_position

spec.doc: Time-weighted average YES price in bps over the trailing `window_secs`, floored. Rejects a zero window (`InvalidAmount`). A window reaching before the oldest observation fails with `ObservationTooOld`; a window extending past `close_time` keeps averaging the final price, because the accumulator only moves when trades are possible.
spec.name: twap

spec.doc: Invalid or unresolvable market. Allowed any time before finality.
spec.name: void_market

spec.doc: True when a `buy` of `collateral_in` would be rejected by the market's breakers right now. Read-only: never writes band state, so on a fresh ledger the reference is taken as the current price — the same value a subsequent real trade would use.
spec.name: would_trip

spec.doc: Temporary (one ledger) band reference for a market.
spec.name: BandState

spec.doc: One market's outcome inside a `BatchResult`, in request order.
spec.name: BatchItem

spec.doc: Result of `redeem_many` / `claim_pool_remainders`: `total` is the single aggregated transfer, `items` has one entry per requested market in the same order.
spec.name: BatchResult

spec.doc: Per-market result of a batch settlement. This union stands in for the `Option<SkipReason>` sketched in the issue: a `#[contracttype]` struct field of type `Option<CustomType>` does not compile under the `testutils` feature (on for every `cargo test` build). The derive emits an xdr conversion gated on `CustomType: Into<ScVal>`, but `#[contracttype]` enums only derive `TryFrom`, and the missing impls cannot be supplied from this crate: `From<Enum> for ScVal` collides with the derive's own `TryFrom` through core's blanket impl (E0119), and `TryFrom<&Option<Enum>> for ScVal` violates the orphan rule (E0117). The union carries the same information and surfaces as a discriminated union in the generated TS bindings.
spec.name: BatchStatus

spec.doc: Per-market circuit breakers, snapshotted at creation from `DataKey::DefaultBreaker`. 0 disables each check. A market without a `Breaker` entry (created before breakers existed) is never checked.

fields.doc: Maximum |post-price - ledger-open price| cumulative movement in bps.
fields.name: band_bps

fields.doc: Maximum |post-price - pre-price| a single trade may move in bps.
fields.name: max_impact_bps

spec.name: BreakerConfig

spec.doc: Binds a market to a reusable committee registry subject to rotation bounds.
spec.name: CommitteeRef

spec.doc: Attested resolution whose proposal can be challenged with a bond during the dispute window. Hashed as `ResolutionSpec::SignersDisputable`, a separate variant, so existing `Signers` commitments are unaffected.

fields.doc: Collateral escrowed by `dispute`; must be positive.
fields.name: dispute_bond

fields.doc: Seconds after a dispute opens before anyone may void it unresolved.
fields.name: escalation_timeout

spec.name: DisputableSignerConfig

tuple_v0.doc: `k` of these members, through `escalation_attest`. Must be disjoint from the proposing signers.
tuple_v0.name: Committee

spec.doc: Who rules on a dispute.
spec.name: Escalation

spec.doc: Fee destination and split, snapshotted per market at creation as a side entry (`DataKey::FeeTerms`) so `Market`'s XDR shape never changes. Markets created before this entry existed have no `FeeTerms` and keep the legacy behaviour: `sweep_fees` pays whatever `DataKey::Treasury` holds at sweep time, with the protocol keeping 100% of the fee. That fallback is documented in `sweep_fees` and makes the upgrade migration-free.

fields.doc: Protocol's share of each trade fee in bps; the rest is the LP's. 0..=BPS. At BPS (the default) the split is exactly today's behaviour.
fields.name: protocol_share_bps

fields.doc: Where the protocol's fee share is swept. Frozen at creation: later `set_treasury` calls never redirect fees already earned.
fields.name: recipient

spec.name: FeeTerms

spec.doc: Dual-path resolution mode: price feed first, falling back to signers.
spec.name: HybridConfig

fields.doc: Unix seconds (ledger timestamp). Trading stops at this time.
fields.name: close_time

fields.doc: Snapshot of the fee at creation so later config changes never move it.
fields.name: fee_bps

fields.doc: Trading fees waiting for `sweep_fees`.
fields.name: fees_accrued

fields.doc: Creator has withdrawn the pool remainder after finality.
fields.name: lp_claimed

fields.doc: IPFS CID / URI of the question metadata.
fields.name: meta_uri

fields.doc: sha256 of the canonical question JSON stored off-chain (IPFS), so a client can prove the text it shows is the text that was committed.
fields.name: question_hash

fields.doc: Commitment to how this market will be resolved, fixed at creation so the creator cannot pick favorable resolution rules after seeing trading activity. The resolver contract verifies a revealed spec against this hash before configuring itself for the market. See `docs/adr/0001-resolution-commitment.md`.
fields.name: resolution_hash

fields.doc: Complete sets in existence == collateral locked for this market.
fields.name: sets_minted

void_v0.doc: Trading allowed until `close_time`, then waiting for the resolver.
void_v0.name: Open

void_v0.doc: Invalid market. Every share redeems at 0.5.
void_v0.name: Void

spec.doc: One point in the TWAP ring buffer. At most one per distinct timestamp.

fields.doc: `OracleState::price_cumulative` as of `ts`.
fields.name: cumulative

spec.name: Observation

spec.doc: Per-market TWAP accumulator (issue #11). Lives in its own entry so the `Market` XDR stays unchanged. Semantics: at the start of every trade the price that held since the last trade is folded into `price_cumulative` over the elapsed interval; the post-trade price then becomes `last_price_bps` until the next trade. That is the Uniswap-v2 model, and it is what makes manipulation expensive — moving the average requires holding the price away from fair value across one or more ledger boundaries, not just within a single transaction. Overflow analysis: `last_price_bps <= 10_000` and each interval adds `price * dt` seconds. A 100-year market lifetime accumulates at most `10_000 * 3.2e9 ~ 3.2e13`; even a pathological `dt = u64::MAX` gives `1.8e19 * 1e4 = 1.8e23`. `i128::MAX` is ~1.7e38, so there is no feasible lifetime that overflows — and every step is `checked_*` anyway, so a violation rejects the transaction instead of corrupting the accumulator.

fields.doc: YES price in bps as of the most recent trade.
fields.name: last_price_bps

fields.doc: Timestamp the accumulator was last advanced to (the timestamp of the most recent trade). The last traded price holds from here onward.
fields.name: last_ts

fields.doc: Observations written so far, capped at `ORACLE_RING`.
fields.name: obs_count

fields.doc: Ring slot of the newest observation, in `0..ORACLE_RING`.
fields.name: obs_index

fields.doc: Running sum of `last_price_bps * seconds_elapsed` since creation.
fields.name: price_cumulative

spec.name: OracleState

spec.doc: A proposed admin handover (#62). Absent when no transfer is pending.
spec.name: PendingAdmin

spec.doc: The full resolution rule a market's `resolution_hash` commits to. Hashing this (rather than the bare `PriceConfig`/`SignerConfig`) keeps the two modes in disjoint hash spaces even if their field encodings could otherwise collide. See `docs/adr/0001-resolution-commitment.md`.
spec.name: ResolutionSpec

spec.doc: Versioned commitment envelope. Unlike a bare [`ResolutionSpec`] it binds the network and the market-core instance, and carries a creator-chosen `salt` that makes a pre-reveal brute-force of the (low-entropy) rule infeasible.

fields.doc: `sha256(network passphrase)`, i.e. `env.ledger().network_id()`.
fields.name: network_id

spec.name: ResolutionSpecV2

spec.doc: Per-market settlement bookkeeping (issue #14). Lives in its own entry so the `Market` XDR stays unchanged.

fields.doc: `finalize_market` has swept the market's remaining balance; no redemption or claim can ever pay out again.
fields.name: closed

fields.doc: Timestamp of `resolve` / `void_market`; 0 while the market is Open.
fields.name: finalized_at

fields.doc: Redemption window, snapshotted at creation from the admin default. `redeem_deadline = finalized_at + horizon_secs`.
fields.name: horizon_secs

fields.doc: Outcome shares held outside the pool (user positions), still redeemable. `redeem` decrements the redeeming holder's shares on both sides, so a losing-side redemption (payout 0) still clears here.
fields.name: outstanding_yes

fields.doc: Collateral already paid to holders and the LP (`redeem` + `claim_pool_remainder` payouts); tracks what has left the market.
fields.name: paid_out

spec.name: SettleState

spec.name: SkipReason

fields.name: pubkey

fields.doc: Total weight that must sign one outcome. Choose it above half the total weight so two outcomes can never both reach it.
fields.name: weight_threshold

cases.doc: Inbound collateral transfer delivered fewer (or different) units than expected, e.g. a fee-on-transfer or under-delivering token (#137).
